svg.text: Spring Boot REST API — Product Catalog (single service, CRUD)
One reference diagram: Maven module tree · UML class diagram (standard notation) · layered request flow · end-to-end trace. Designed to be zoomed into.
solid line, filled head = association (holds a permanent reference)
dashed line, open head = dependency (uses briefly: accepts / returns / throws)
dashed line, hollow triangle = realization / implements (interface)
+ public - private · «@Annotation» = Spring stereotype · box = name / attributes / operations
Layer colour coding (consistent across all views)
Single Spring Boot module. Package colours match the class boxes and flow nodes.
Runnable jar: java -jar product-api.jar → embedded Tomcat
2 · UML class diagram — layered class chain
«@RestController» → «@Service» (behind an interface) → «@Repository» → «@Entity», with DTOs, a mapper and centralised exception handling.
inherited: save, findById, findAll, deleteById, count ...
keeps entities out of the web layer
thrown by service when an id is missing
3 · Layered request flow — how one HTTP call travels through the stack
return: ResultSet → Product → ProductMapper → ProductResponse → Jackson JSON
@Transactional · commit on success, rollback on error
4 · Request trace — POST /api/products (create) · badges ①…⑨ map onto Region 3

g.text: Client sends POST /api/products with a JSON body over HTTP :8080.
DispatcherServlet matches the route and dispatches to ProductController.create() (@PostMapping).
Jackson deserialises JSON → ProductRequest; @Valid runs Bean Validation (400 if it fails).
Controller delegates to productService.create(req) through the ProductService interface.
ProductServiceImpl (@Transactional) uses ProductMapper.toEntity() to build a Product.
Calls productRepository.save(product) → Hibernate emits INSERT over a HikariCP connection.
DB returns the generated id; the transaction commits when the service method returns.
Mapper.toResponse() → ProductResponse; controller returns 201 Created + Location header.

svg.text: Jackson serialises the DTO back to JSON; the client gets the response.
• GET /api/products/{id} with a missing id → service throws
• Everything runs in one JVM; no network hops between layers —
method calls, not REST/Feign like a microservice system.
• Layered rule: Controller → Service → Repository only; the web
layer never touches the entity directly (DTOs cross the boundary).
Single self-contained SVG · viewBox 2560×2100 (rendered 5120×4200) · layer-coloured across tree, class diagram and flow · standard UML notation.
